files.compose.yml:
# ELVIRA on Docker Compose.
#
# The catalog always runs. Everything else is a profile, switched on in .env:
#
#   COMPOSE_PROFILES=postgres,redis,lending
#
#   postgres    PostgreSQL on this machine (leave out to use your own: PGHOST in .env)
#   redis       Redis on this machine (leave out to use your own: REDIS_HOST in .env)
#   lending     Readium LCP license server and the lcpencrypt worker
#   ocr         OCR for scanned PDFs                                    (develop images, amd64)
#   search      embedding service for search by meaning                 (develop images, amd64)
#   extraction  paragraphs, tables, figures and formulas from PDFs     (develop images, amd64)
#   assistant   Ollama for the reading assistant
#   mail        MailDev, catches e-mails for testing
#   telemetry   Grafana with Tempo, Loki and Mimir
#
# .env holds every setting (see .env.example). Run docker compose from this directory.

x-worker: &worker
  restart: unless-stopped
  volumes:
    - data:/var/local/evilflowers

services:
  # ------------------------------------------------------------------ catalog (always)
  evilflowers:
    image: ${ELVIRA_CATALOG_IMAGE:-ghcr.io/evilflowerscatalog/evilflowerscatalog:master}
    restart: unless-stopped
    env_file: [.env]
    # The admin assets are collected into ./static at every start; nginx serves them from there.
    # Then the image's own start: migrate, load languages, run everything under supervisord.
    command: [/bin/sh, -c, "python3 manage.py collectstatic --noinput --verbosity 0 && exec conf/entrypoint.sh"]
    # Loopback only: nginx on this machine is the way in (ELVIRA_HTTP_BIND=0.0.0.0 to change).
    ports: ["${ELVIRA_HTTP_BIND:-127.0.0.1}:8000:8000"]
    volumes:
      - data:/var/local/evilflowers
      - ./static:/usr/src/app/static
    depends_on:
      postgres: {condition: service_healthy, required: false}
      redis: {condition: service_healthy, required: false}
    stop_grace_period: 60s

  # ------------------------------------------------------------------ data
  postgres:
    profiles: [postgres]
    # PostgreSQL 18 with pgvector and pg_search.
    image: ghcr.io/evilflowerscatalog/evilflowers-postgresql:18
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: ${PGDATABASE}
      POSTGRES_USER: ${PGUSER}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${PGPASSWORD}
    volumes:
      # PostgreSQL 18 keeps its data in /var/lib/postgresql/18/docker.
      - postgres:/var/lib/postgresql
    shm_size: 1g
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "pg_isready", "-h", "127.0.0.1", "-U", "${PGUSER}", "-d", "${PGDATABASE}"]
      interval: 10s
      retries: 10

  redis:
    profiles: [redis]
    # Celery broker (db 7) and the catalog's cache (db 1).
    image: redis:7
    restart: unless-stopped
    volumes:
      - redis:/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "ping"]
      interval: 10s
      retries: 10

  # ------------------------------------------------------------------ lending
  readium:
    profiles: [lending]
    # License (8989) and Status (8990) servers. Readers never reach them: the catalog proxies
    # licences, status documents and encrypted content under /readium/v1/.
    image: ghcr.io/evilflowerscatalog/readium-lcp-server:master
    restart: unless-stopped
    volumes:
      - data:/var/local/evilflowers
      - readium:/usr/local/var/readium/db
      # Written by scripts/setup.sh (or downloaded from elvira.digital/deploy).
      - ./readium/config.yaml:/usr/local/etc/readium/config.yaml:ro
      - ./readium/htpasswd:/usr/local/etc/readium/htpasswd:ro
      # Your production certificate from EDRLab, if you have one (see ELVIRA_LCP_* in .env).
      - ./readium/certs:/usr/local/etc/readium/certs:ro
      # Both servers' logs to docker logs instead of files inside the container.
      - ./readium/supervisord.conf:/etc/supervisord.conf:ro

  lcpencrypt:
    <<: *worker
    profiles: [lending]
    # Encrypts each lent title and registers it with the license server.
    image: ${ELVIRA_LCPENCRYPT_IMAGE:-ghcr.io/evilflowerscatalog/evilflowers-lcpencrypt-worker:master}
    environment:
      BROKER: ${CELERY_BROKER_URL}
      STORAGE_PATH: /var/local/evilflowers
      BROKER_VISIBILITY_TIMEOUT: "43200"
      # Node name, in full: the image's health check pings exactly this.
      CELERY_HOSTNAME: lcpencrypt@elvira

  # ------------------------------------------------------------------ OCR
  ocr:
    <<: *worker
    profiles: [ocr]
    # ocrmypdf and Tesseract. Runs as root: it creates <entry>/ocr/ in directories the catalog owns.
    image: ghcr.io/evilflowerscatalog/evilflowers-ocr-service:master
    platform: linux/amd64
    user: "0:0"
    command: [celery, -A, evilflowers_ocr_worker.worker, worker, --loglevel=INFO, -E, --concurrency=1, --queues=evilflowers_ocr_worker, --hostname=ocr@%h]
    environment:
      BROKER: ${CELERY_BROKER_URL}
      STORAGE_PATH: /var/local/evilflowers
      BROKER_VISIBILITY_TIMEOUT: "43200"
      OCR_JOBS: "2"
    tmpfs: [/tmp]

  # ------------------------------------------------------------------ search
  tei-embed:
    profiles: [search]
    # Text Embeddings Inference serving the model the catalog is built for (2.3 GB on first start).
    image: ghcr.io/huggingface/text-embeddings-inference:cpu-1.9.4
    platform: linux/amd64
    restart: unless-stopped
    command:
      - --model-id=intfloat/multilingual-e5-large-instruct
      - --revision=274baa43b0e13e37fafa6428dbc7938e62e5c439
      - --port=80
    environment:
      API_KEY: ${EVILFLOWERS_EMBEDDING_API_KEY}
    volumes:
      - tei:/data

  # ------------------------------------------------------------------ extraction
  # Four workers that post their results to the catalog as a service user (EXTRACTION_API_KEY,
  # README: "Extraction"). amd64 images.
  analyzer:
    <<: *worker
    profiles: [extraction]
    image: ghcr.io/evilflowerscatalog/evilflowers-analyzer-service:develop
    platform: linux/amd64
    command: [celery, -A, evilflowers_analyzer.worker, worker, --loglevel=INFO, -E, --concurrency=1, --queues=evilflowers_analyzer, --hostname=analyzer@%h]
    environment: &extraction-env
      REDIS_URL: ${CELERY_BROKER_URL}
      STORAGE_PATH: /var/local/evilflowers
      CATALOG_API_URL: http://evilflowers:8000
      CATALOG_API_KEY: ${EXTRACTION_API_KEY}
      BROKER_VISIBILITY_TIMEOUT: "43200"
      HF_HOME: /models
      LAYOUT_THREADS: "2"
      OMP_NUM_THREADS: "2"
      LAYOUT_BATCH_PAGES: "8"
    volumes: &extraction-volumes
      - data:/var/local/evilflowers
      - models:/models
    tmpfs: [/tmp]

  image:
    <<: *worker
    profiles: [extraction]
    image: ghcr.io/evilflowerscatalog/evilflowers-image-service:develop
    platform: linux/amd64
    command: [celery, -A, evilflowers_image.worker, worker, --loglevel=INFO, -E, --concurrency=1, --queues=evilflowers_image, --hostname=image@%h]
    environment:
      <<: *extraction-env
      CAPTIONS_ENABLED: "0"
    volumes: *extraction-volumes
    tmpfs: [/tmp]

  equation:
    <<: *worker
    profiles: [extraction]
    image: ghcr.io/evilflowerscatalog/evilflowers-equation-service:develop
    platform: linux/amd64
    command: [celery, -A, evilflowers_equation.worker, worker, --loglevel=INFO, -E, --concurrency=1, --queues=evilflowers_equation, --hostname=equation@%h]
    environment:
      <<: *extraction-env
      MODELS_PATH: /models/latex-ocr
      LATEX_THREADS: "1"
      LATEX_WORKERS: "2"
    volumes: *extraction-volumes
    tmpfs: [/tmp]

  text:
    <<: *worker
    profiles: [extraction]
    image: ghcr.io/evilflowerscatalog/evilflowers-text-service:develop
    platform: linux/amd64
    command: [celery, -A, evilflowers_text.worker, worker, --loglevel=INFO, -E, --concurrency=1, "--queues=evilflowers.text.paragraphs,evilflowers.text.tables,evilflowers_text_worker", --hostname=text@%h]
    environment:
      <<: *extraction-env
      TEI_URL: ${EVILFLOWERS_EMBEDDING_URL}
      TEI_API_KEY: ${EVILFLOWERS_EMBEDDING_API_KEY}
      TEI_BATCH_SIZE: "8"
      TABLE_REVIEW_ENABLED: "false"
    tmpfs: [/tmp]

  # ------------------------------------------------------------------ assistant
  ollama:
    profiles: [assistant]
    # Starts empty: pull the model once (README: "Assistant"). The default needs ~25 GB of RAM.
    image: ollama/ollama:0.40.15
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE: "-1"
      OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH: "32768"
      OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION: "1"
    volumes:
      - ollama:/root/.ollama

  # ------------------------------------------------------------------ testing and operations
  maildev:
    profiles: [mail]
    # Catches every e-mail the catalog sends. Inbox on http://127.0.0.1:1080.
    image: maildev/maildev:2.2.1
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports: ["127.0.0.1:1080:1080"]

  otel-lgtm:
    profiles: [telemetry]
    # OpenTelemetry collector, Tempo, Loki, Mimir and Grafana (http://127.0.0.1:3000, admin/admin).
    image: grafana/otel-lgtm:0.39.0
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports: ["127.0.0.1:3000:3000"]

volumes:
  data: {}
  postgres: {}
  redis: {}
  readium: {}
  tei: {}
  models: {}
  ollama: {}
files..env.example:
# ELVIRA settings: one file for Docker Compose, plain Docker and Kubernetes.
#
#   cp .env.example .env     then set your addresses and profiles below
#   scripts/setup.sh         fills in every change-me secret and writes the nginx and readium files
#
# elvira.digital/deploy writes the same file for you, with the secrets made in your browser.
# Never commit .env: it holds your secrets.

# =================================================================== what runs
# Profiles to start, comma-separated (compose.yml lists them all).
COMPOSE_PROFILES=postgres,redis
COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=elvira

# :master = stable, :develop = development images (search, OCR, extraction).
ELVIRA_CATALOG_IMAGE=ghcr.io/evilflowerscatalog/evilflowerscatalog:master
ELVIRA_LCPENCRYPT_IMAGE=ghcr.io/evilflowerscatalog/evilflowers-lcpencrypt-worker:master

# =================================================================== addresses
# Where readers and apps reach the catalog, and where the portal is served from (empty = no portal).
ELVIRA_DOMAIN=library.example.org
ELVIRA_PORTAL_DOMAIN=portal.example.org
# 127.0.0.1 with nginx on this machine; 0.0.0.0 if your proxy runs elsewhere.
ELVIRA_HTTP_BIND=127.0.0.1
# Where this directory lives on the server (nginx serves its static/), and the built portal.
ELVIRA_DIR=/opt/elvira
ELVIRA_PORTAL_ROOT=/var/www/elvira-portal

# The same addresses as the catalog reads them.
INSTANCE_NAME=library.example.org
ALLOWED_HOSTS=library.example.org;evilflowers
EVILFLOWERS_BASE_URL=https://library.example.org
EVILFLOWERS_READIUM_BASE_URL=https://library.example.org
EVILFLOWERS_PORTAL_URL=https://portal.example.org
# The only browser origin allowed to call the API.
CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=https://portal.example.org
EVILFLOWERS_CONTACT_EMAIL=library@example.org

# =================================================================== catalog
DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=evil_flowers_catalog.settings.production
SECRET_KEY=change-me
# RSA private key (JWK, one line) that signs access tokens.
SECURED_VIEW_JWK=change-me
GUNICORN_CMD_ARGS=-w 4 -b 0.0.0.0:8000 --keep-alive 75
# One proxy (nginx) in front appends to X-Forwarded-For.
EVILFLOWERS_RATE_LIMIT_PROXY_COUNT=1
EVILFLOWERS_LOG_FORMAT=json
EVILFLOWERS_STORAGE_DRIVER=apps.files.storage.filesystem.FileSystemStorage
EVILFLOWERS_STORAGE_FILESYSTEM_DATADIR=/var/local/evilflowers

# =================================================================== PostgreSQL
# postgres = the bundled one (profile postgres); your own server's name otherwise.
PGHOST=postgres
PGPORT=5432
PGDATABASE=evilflowers
PGUSER=evilflowers
PGPASSWORD=change-me

# =================================================================== Redis and Celery
# redis = the bundled one (profile redis); your own server's name otherwise.
REDIS_HOST=redis
REDIS_PORT=6379
REDIS_DATABASE=1
CELERY_BROKER_URL=redis://redis:6379/7
CELERY_RESULT_BACKEND=redis://redis:6379/7
CELERY_BROKER_VISIBILITY_TIMEOUT=43200
CELERY_WORKER_CONCURRENCY=2
# The one worker also runs the nightly maintenance (backups, cleanup).
EVILFLOWERS_MAINTENANCE_QUEUE=celery
EVILFLOWERS_EVENT_BROKER_EXECUTOR=apps.events.services.CeleryEventExecutionService
EVILFLOWERS_EVENT_BROKER_TRANSFORMER=apps.events.transformers.DjangoTransformer

# =================================================================== MCP server for AI agents (/mcp/v1)
EVILFLOWERS_MCP_ENABLED=1
EVILFLOWERS_MCP_AUTHENTICATION_SCHEMAS=Bearer

# =================================================================== lending (profile lending)
# User and password of the license servers (readium/htpasswd and the two URLs below).
ELVIRA_READIUM_USER=evilflowers
ELVIRA_READIUM_PASSWORD=change-me
EVILFLOWERS_READIUM_LCPSV_URL=http://evilflowers:change-me@readium:8989
EVILFLOWERS_READIUM_LSDSV_URL=http://evilflowers:change-me@readium:8990
EVILFLOWERS_READIUM_LCPENCRYPT_NOTIFY_URL=http://evilflowers:8000/readium/v1/hooks/encryption
EVILFLOWERS_READIUM_LCPENCRYPT_REPORT_URL=http://evilflowers:8000/readium/v1/hooks/encryption/result
# EDRLab's test certificate, built into the image: only test builds of reading apps open its books.
# Production: put EDRLab's cert.pem and privkey.pem in readium/certs/ and use
#   ELVIRA_LCP_PROFILE=1.0
#   ELVIRA_LCP_CERT=/usr/local/etc/readium/certs/cert.pem
#   ELVIRA_LCP_KEY=/usr/local/etc/readium/certs/privkey.pem
ELVIRA_LCP_PROFILE=basic
ELVIRA_LCP_CERT=/usr/local/var/readium/lcp/cert/cert-edrlab-test.pem
ELVIRA_LCP_KEY=/usr/local/var/readium/lcp/cert/privkey-edrlab-test.pem

# =================================================================== OCR (profile ocr, develop)
EVILFLOWERS_OCR_ENABLED=false
EVILFLOWERS_OCR_QUEUE=evilflowers_ocr_worker

# =================================================================== search by meaning (profile search, develop)
# http://tei-embed with the profile, your own service's URL otherwise, empty = words only.
EVILFLOWERS_EMBEDDING_URL=
EVILFLOWERS_EMBEDDING_MODEL=intfloat/multilingual-e5-large-instruct@274baa43b0e13e37fafa6428dbc7938e62e5c439
EVILFLOWERS_EMBEDDING_API_KEY=change-me

# =================================================================== extraction (profile extraction, develop)
EVILFLOWERS_EXTRACTION_ENABLED=0
# API key of the catalog's extraction service user: scripts/extraction-api-key.py prints one.
EXTRACTION_API_KEY=

# =================================================================== reading assistant (profile assistant, or your Ollama API)
EVILFLOWERS_ASSISTANT_ENABLED=0
EVILFLOWERS_ASSISTANT_OLLAMA_ENDPOINT=http://ollama:11434/api/chat
EVILFLOWERS_ASSISTANT_OLLAMA_MODEL=qwen3.6:35b-a3b-q4_K_M
EVILFLOWERS_ASSISTANT_OLLAMA_API_KEY=
EVILFLOWERS_ASSISTANT_OLLAMA_THINK=0
EVILFLOWERS_ASSISTANT_OLLAMA_NUM_CTX=32768

# =================================================================== e-mail
# maildev with the profile mail (port 1025, no TLS); your SMTP server otherwise.
EVILFLOWERS_NOTIFICATIONS_ENABLED=false
EMAIL_HOST=
EMAIL_PORT=587
EMAIL_USE_TLS=true
EMAIL_HOST_USER=
EMAIL_HOST_PASSWORD=
DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL=library@example.org

# =================================================================== nightly database backup to S3
# Empty schedule = no backup.
EVILFLOWERS_BACKUP_SCHEDULE=
EVILFLOWERS_BACKUP_DESTINATION=s3://backups/evilflowers
EVILFLOWERS_BACKUP_S3_HOST=s3.example.org
EVILFLOWERS_BACKUP_S3_SECURE=1
EVILFLOWERS_BACKUP_S3_ACCESS_KEY=
EVILFLOWERS_BACKUP_S3_SECRET_KEY=

# =================================================================== traces, metrics and logs
# http://otel-lgtm:4318 with the profile telemetry, your collector otherwise.
OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=
OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES=service.namespace=elvira,deployment.environment.name=production
files.readium/config.yaml.tmpl:
# Readium LCP License (lcp) and Status (lsd) servers. scripts/setup.sh writes
# readium/config.yaml from this template with the values in .env.
#
# Every public link points at the catalog, which proxies licences, status documents and
# encrypted content under /readium/v1/: readers never reach ports 8989/8990.

# "basic" accepts EDRLab's test certificate; production certificates from EDRLab need "1.0".
profile: "${ELVIRA_LCP_PROFILE}"

lcp:
  host: "0.0.0.0"
  port: 8989
  public_base_url: "https://${ELVIRA_DOMAIN}/readium/v1"
  database: "sqlite3://file:/usr/local/var/readium/db/lcp.sqlite?cache=shared&mode=rwc"
  auth_file: "/usr/local/etc/readium/htpasswd"

lsd:
  host: "0.0.0.0"
  port: 8990
  public_base_url: "https://${ELVIRA_DOMAIN}/readium/v1"
  database: "sqlite3://file:/usr/local/var/readium/db/lsd.sqlite?cache=shared&mode=rwc"
  auth_file: "/usr/local/etc/readium/htpasswd"
  license_link_url: "https://${ELVIRA_DOMAIN}/readium/v1/licenses/{license_id}.lcpl"

certificate:
  cert: "${ELVIRA_LCP_CERT}"
  private_key: "${ELVIRA_LCP_KEY}"

license:
  links:
    status: "https://${ELVIRA_DOMAIN}/readium/v1/licenses/{license_id}/status"
    hint: "https://${ELVIRA_DOMAIN}/readium/v1/hint"
    publication: "https://${ELVIRA_DOMAIN}/readium/v1/content/{publication_id}"

# lcpencrypt writes the encrypted copies into the shared data volume.
storage:
  mode: "fs"
  filesystem:
    directory: "/var/local/evilflowers"

license_status:
  register: true
  renew: true
  return: true
  renting_days: 14
  renew_days: 14

# The status server tells the license server about returns and renewals with these.
lsd_notify_auth:
  username: "${ELVIRA_READIUM_USER}"
  password: "${ELVIRA_READIUM_PASSWORD}"
lcp_update_auth:
  username: "${ELVIRA_READIUM_USER}"
  password: "${ELVIRA_READIUM_PASSWORD}"
files.readium/supervisord.conf:
; The readium image's supervisord, with both servers' output on the container's stdout/stderr
; (the image writes them to files under /var/log/readium, invisible to docker logs).
[supervisord]
nodaemon=true
user=root
logfile=/dev/null
logfile_maxbytes=0

[program:lsd]
directory=/usr/local/var/readium
command=/usr/local/bin/lsdserver
autostart=true
autorestart=true
priority=900
stdout_logfile=/dev/fd/1
stdout_logfile_maxbytes=0
stderr_logfile=/dev/fd/2
stderr_logfile_maxbytes=0

[program:lcp]
directory=/usr/local/var/readium
command=/usr/local/bin/lcpserver
autostart=true
autorestart=true
priority=900
stdout_logfile=/dev/fd/1
stdout_logfile_maxbytes=0
stderr_logfile=/dev/fd/2
stderr_logfile_maxbytes=0
files.docker/run.sh:
#!/bin/sh
# ELVIRA with plain docker run: the catalog, and PostgreSQL and Redis unless .env points at your
# own (PGHOST, REDIS_HOST). Same .env as Docker Compose. For lending, OCR, search, extraction and
# the rest, use Docker Compose (compose.yml): it is the same set of containers with profiles.
#
#   docker/run.sh up        start (or update) everything
#   docker/run.sh down      stop and remove the containers (volumes stay)
#   docker/run.sh status    what is running
set -eu

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
[ -f .env ] || { echo "No .env here: run scripts/setup.sh first." >&2; exit 1; }

# Values from .env, read line by line: the file is not shell syntax (the JWK holds braces).
env_value() { grep -E "^$1=" .env | tail -n 1 | cut -d= -f2-; }

PREFIX=elvira
NET=$PREFIX
IMAGE=$(env_value ELVIRA_CATALOG_IMAGE)
BIND=$(env_value ELVIRA_HTTP_BIND)

# run <service> <docker run options…> <image> [command…]: the container elvira-<service>, reachable
# as <service> on the network (the same names compose.yml uses).
run() {
  service=$1; shift
  docker rm -f "$PREFIX-$service" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  docker run -d --name "$PREFIX-$service" --network "$NET" --network-alias "$service" --restart unless-stopped "$@" >/dev/null
  echo "started $PREFIX-$service"
}

wait_healthy() {
  printf 'waiting for %s' "$1"
  until [ "$(docker inspect -f '{{.State.Health.Status}}' "$PREFIX-$1" 2>/dev/null)" = healthy ]; do
    printf .; sleep 2
  done
  echo
}

up() {
  docker network inspect "$NET" >/dev/null 2>&1 || docker network create "$NET" >/dev/null
  if [ "$(env_value PGHOST)" = postgres ]; then
    run postgres \
      -e POSTGRES_DB="$(env_value PGDATABASE)" -e POSTGRES_USER="$(env_value PGUSER)" -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD="$(env_value PGPASSWORD)" \
      -v "$PREFIX-postgres:/var/lib/postgresql" --shm-size 1g \
      --health-cmd "pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 -U $(env_value PGUSER)" --health-interval 5s \
      ghcr.io/evilflowerscatalog/evilflowers-postgresql:18
    wait_healthy postgres
  fi
  if [ "$(env_value REDIS_HOST)" = redis ]; then
    run redis -v "$PREFIX-redis:/data" --health-cmd "redis-cli ping" --health-interval 5s redis:7
    wait_healthy redis
  fi
  docker pull -q "$IMAGE" >/dev/null
  # Same as compose.yml: collect the admin assets into ./static, then the image's own start.
  run evilflowers --env-file .env \
    -p "${BIND:-127.0.0.1}:8000:8000" \
    -v "$PREFIX-data:/var/local/evilflowers" -v "$PWD/static:/usr/src/app/static" \
    "$IMAGE" /bin/sh -c "python3 manage.py collectstatic --noinput --verbosity 0 && exec conf/entrypoint.sh"
  wait_healthy evilflowers
  echo "The catalog answers on http://${BIND:-127.0.0.1}:8000"
}

down() {
  for c in evilflowers redis postgres; do
    if docker rm -f "$PREFIX-$c" >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "removed $PREFIX-$c"; fi
  done
}

case "${1:-}" in
  up) up ;;
  down) down ;;
  status) docker ps --filter "name=^$PREFIX-" --format 'table {{.Names}}\t{{.Status}}\t{{.Ports}}' ;;
  *) sed -n '2,10p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 2 ;;
esac
files.k8s/base/catalog.yaml:
# The catalog: gunicorn, Celery worker, scheduler and event listener under supervisord in one pod
# (the image's own start), with every setting from the elvira-env Secret (.env).
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: data
spec:
  # Publications, covers, encrypted copies, extraction crops. Every worker mounts it: keep them on
  # one node with ReadWriteOnce, or use a ReadWriteMany storage class.
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  resources: {requests: {storage: 20Gi}}
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: evilflowers
  labels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: evilflowers, app.kubernetes.io/part-of: elvira}
spec:
  replicas: 1
  strategy: {type: Recreate}
  selector:
    matchLabels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: evilflowers}
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: evilflowers, app.kubernetes.io/part-of: elvira}
    spec:
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 60
      containers:
        - name: evilflowers
          image: ghcr.io/evilflowerscatalog/evilflowerscatalog:master
          envFrom:
            - secretRef: {name: elvira-env}
          ports:
            - {name: http, containerPort: 8000}
          # Migrations and supervisord start first: give it five minutes.
          startupProbe: {tcpSocket: {port: http}, periodSeconds: 10, failureThreshold: 30}
          readinessProbe: {tcpSocket: {port: http}, periodSeconds: 10}
          livenessProbe: {tcpSocket: {port: http}, periodSeconds: 30}
          volumeMounts:
            - {name: data, mountPath: /var/local/evilflowers}
      volumes:
        - name: data
          persistentVolumeClaim: {claimName: data}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: evilflowers
spec:
  selector: {app.kubernetes.io/name: evilflowers}
  ports:
    - {name: http, port: 8000, targetPort: http}
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: evilflowers
  annotations:
    # ingress-nginx; other controllers have their own names for the same limits.
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-body-size: 500m
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-read-timeout: "300"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-send-timeout: "300"
spec:
  # Add ingressClassName and a tls block for your cluster in config/k8s/kustomization.yaml.
  rules:
    - host: library.example.org
      http:
        paths:
          - path: /
            pathType: Prefix
            backend:
              service: {name: evilflowers, port: {name: http}}

apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: readium
spec:
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  resources: {requests: {storage: 1Gi}}
---
# The same file as readium/supervisord.conf (a test keeps them equal): both servers' logs to the
# pod log instead of files inside the container.
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: readium-supervisord
data:
  supervisord.conf: |
    ; The readium image's supervisord, with both servers' output on the container's stdout/stderr
    ; (the image writes them to files under /var/log/readium, invisible to docker logs).
    [supervisord]
    nodaemon=true
    user=root
    logfile=/dev/null
    logfile_maxbytes=0

    [program:lsd]
    directory=/usr/local/var/readium
    command=/usr/local/bin/lsdserver
    autostart=true
    autorestart=true
    priority=900
    stdout_logfile=/dev/fd/1
    stdout_logfile_maxbytes=0
    stderr_logfile=/dev/fd/2
    stderr_logfile_maxbytes=0

    [program:lcp]
    directory=/usr/local/var/readium
    command=/usr/local/bin/lcpserver
    autostart=true
    autorestart=true
    priority=900
    stdout_logfile=/dev/fd/1
    stdout_logfile_maxbytes=0
    stderr_logfile=/dev/fd/2
    stderr_logfile_maxbytes=0
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: readium
  labels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: readium, app.kubernetes.io/part-of: elvira}
spec:
  replicas: 1
  strategy: {type: Recreate}
  selector:
    matchLabels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: readium}
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: readium, app.kubernetes.io/part-of: elvira}
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: readium
          image: ghcr.io/evilflowerscatalog/readium-lcp-server:master
          ports:
            - {name: lcp, containerPort: 8989}
            - {name: lsd, containerPort: 8990}
          readinessProbe: {tcpSocket: {port: lcp}, periodSeconds: 10}
          volumeMounts:
            - {name: data, mountPath: /var/local/evilflowers}
            - {name: readium, mountPath: /usr/local/var/readium/db}
            - {name: config, mountPath: /usr/local/etc/readium/config.yaml, subPath: config.yaml, readOnly: true}
            - {name: config, mountPath: /usr/local/etc/readium/htpasswd, subPath: htpasswd, readOnly: true}
            - {name: supervisord, mountPath: /etc/supervisord.conf, subPath: supervisord.conf, readOnly: true}
      volumes:
        - name: data
          persistentVolumeClaim: {claimName: data}
        - name: readium
          persistentVolumeClaim: {claimName: readium}
        - name: config
          secret: {secretName: readium}
        - name: supervisord
          configMap: {name: readium-supervisord}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: readium
spec:
  selector: {app.kubernetes.io/name: readium}
  ports:
    - {name: lcp, port: 8989, targetPort: lcp}
    - {name: lsd, port: 8990, targetPort: lsd}
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: lcpencrypt
  labels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: lcpencrypt, app.kubernetes.io/part-of: elvira}
spec:
  replicas: 1
  strategy: {type: Recreate}
  selector:
    matchLabels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: lcpencrypt}
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: lcpencrypt, app.kubernetes.io/part-of: elvira}
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: lcpencrypt
          image: ghcr.io/evilflowerscatalog/evilflowers-lcpencrypt-worker:master
          env:
            - name: BROKER
              valueFrom: {secretKeyRef: {name: elvira-env, key: CELERY_BROKER_URL}}
            - {name: STORAGE_PATH, value: /var/local/evilflowers}

          volumeMounts:
            - {name: data, mountPath: /var/local/evilflowers}
      volumes:
        - name: data
          persistentVolumeClaim: {claimName: data}

apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: postgres
spec:
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  resources: {requests: {storage: 10Gi}}
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: postgres
  labels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: postgres, app.kubernetes.io/part-of: elvira}
spec:
  replicas: 1
  strategy: {type: Recreate}
  selector:
    matchLabels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: postgres}
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: postgres, app.kubernetes.io/part-of: elvira}
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: postgres
          image: ghcr.io/evilflowerscatalog/evilflowers-postgresql:18
          env:
            - name: POSTGRES_DB
              valueFrom: {secretKeyRef: {name: elvira-env, key: PGDATABASE}}
            - name: POSTGRES_USER
              valueFrom: {secretKeyRef: {name: elvira-env, key: PGUSER}}
            - name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD
              valueFrom: {secretKeyRef: {name: elvira-env, key: PGPASSWORD}}
          ports:
            - {name: postgres, containerPort: 5432}
          readinessProbe:
            exec: {command: [sh, -c, 'pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -d "$POSTGRES_DB"']}
            periodSeconds: 10
          volumeMounts:
            # PostgreSQL 18 keeps its data in /var/lib/postgresql/18/docker.
            - {name: postgres, mountPath: /var/lib/postgresql}
            - {name: shm, mountPath: /dev/shm}
      volumes:
        - name: postgres
          persistentVolumeClaim: {claimName: postgres}
        - name: shm
          emptyDir: {medium: Memory, sizeLimit: 1Gi}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: postgres
spec:
  selector: {app.kubernetes.io/name: postgres}
  ports:
    - {name: postgres, port: 5432, targetPort: postgres}
